prompt: Which of the following is most likely a violation of human resources regulations:
choices: Paula has to wait 60 days to receive benefits from her new job.
Riley is fired for arriving late to her shift one time.
Luca is sent home early so his employer does not have to pay him overtime.
Devon only interviews male candidates for a managerial position.
explanation: Devon only interviews male candidates for a managerial position. Employment law requires that employers cannot discriminate based on race, gender, age, disability, etc. If Devon does not interview any female candidates for a managerial position, he is likely violating these laws by discriminating on the basis of gender. Devon should interview candidates based on their merits rather than their genders. It is not necessarily a violation of human resources regulation to fire an employee for arriving late. It is also not illegal to send an employee home to avoid paying him overtime. Finally, employers are allowed to impose waiting periods on benefits.

prompt: Ian is starting a business. He wants to be able to make his own decisions quickly, receive tax benefits, and reap all of the rewards for his hard work. Which type of business ownership is best for Ian?
explanation: Sole proprietorship. A sole proprietorship is a business owned by one person who receives all the profits from the business and takes all the risks. In a sole proprietorship, the owner is able to make his/her own decisions quickly, reap the financial benefits of his/her work, and enjoy lower tax rates. Therefore, Ian should start a sole-proprietorship business. Corporations, partnerships, and franchises do not offer the benefits that Ian is looking for in his new businesses.

prompt: Businesses must withhold __________ from employees' paychecks.
explanation: Federal income tax. Every employee must pay federal income tax, but the employer is required to withhold that tax from the employees' wages and pay that amount to the government. Self-employment tax is paid by individuals who work for themselves. It is not withheld from employees' paychecks. Excise tax is tax paid by businesses who produce or use certain types of products. It is not withheld from employees' paychecks. Workers' compensation is a form of insurance that employers purchase to provide benefits to employees who are injured on the job. It is not withheld from employees' paychecks.

prompt: A department store has recently experienced declining store traffic and decreased sales. Many customers complain that the store's displays are cluttered and unexciting—and many people have started shopping at a competing department store. This store may face pressure from its distribution channel partners because
choices: its poor performance will negatively impact its partners' image.
the store is obviously unable to recover from its losses.
it is no longer adding value to the products it is selling.
consumers prefer buying products from successful stores.
explanation: It is no longer adding value to the products it is selling. Every channel member should add value to the product as it moves through the channel. Adding value to the product benefits all channel members. If a member does not add value, channel managers need to reevaluate whether or not that member belongs in the channel. Retailers, for example, are point-of-sale advertising specialists and may create exciting visual displays in their stores to promote a manufacturer's product. If a store fails to promote products successfully, it will likely face pressure from its partners within the channel of distribution. There is not enough information in this example to determine if this store is unable to recover from its losses. Many stores are able to recover from poor performance and increase profits over time. One store's poor performance will not necessarily harm the image of its channel partners. It is not necessarily true that consumers prefer buying products from successful stores. Consumers generally purchase products for a variety of reasons, including price, convenience, and loyalty to a brand—not necessarily because of a particular store's success.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of an industrial user:
choices: A college student buying school supplies
explanation: A construction company buying wood. An industrial user is a business that buys materials, services, or goods that will be used to make other goods or used in the operation of the company. A construction company, for instance, must buy lumber, steel, and other materials needed to build homes and offices. An ultimate consumer, on the other hand, is anyone who personally uses a good or service to satisfy her/his own needs or wants. We are all ultimate consumers of many different goods and services. Examples of ultimate consumers include an individual buying toothpaste, a family buying groceries, and a student buying school supplies.

prompt: A soft-drink producer distributes its products in all retail settings: restaurants, grocery stores, wholesale stores, gas stations, and discount stores. The producer's goal is to make its products easily accessible wherever consumers may go. This is an example of __________ distribution.
explanation: Intensive. There are three main forms of distribution: intensive, selective, and exclusive. Intensive distribution aims to achieve saturation within a market by distributing to all available retailers/outlets. Producers that utilize selective distribution choose a few outlets to distribute their products to, and focus their attention and efforts on those select few. Exclusive distribution involves choosing a single outlet to distribute products to. In this example, intensive distribution is demonstrated.

prompt: When responding to an official request for a formally solicited project, the writer creating the proposal should
choices: provide updates for the approved project.
provide formal objectives to define the proposed project.
follow directions in the request for proposal document.
explain why the project should be continued.
explanation: Follow directions in the request for proposal document. A formally solicited project provides the writer with a request for proposal document (RFP) that provides directions on how to prepare and write the proposal. Since a formally solicited project is already defined by the client, there is no need for the writer to provide any type of objectives to define a proposed project. Updates are provided for ongoing projects. Explanations for continuing a project are given for renewal project proposals.

prompt: A manager who requires employees to create positive customer relations should provide employee training that focuses on
explanation: Courteous and helpful service. Training employees to treat customers in courteous ways will help create positive customer relations that improve a company's image. Safety and health regulations, computer and software skills, and superior production planning can all help a company deliver better customer service, but it is courteous and helpful treatment that customers notice first.

prompt: What type of competitors are two different athletic shoe manufacturers?
explanation: Direct. Direct competitors offer similar types of goods or services to the same target market. Since shoe manufacturers produce similar products, they are direct competitors. Indirect competitors have dissimilar or unrelated businesses. A monopoly is a single business that influences the entire production of a good or service. In market economies, monopolies are usually considered illegal. Oligopolies are industries that have a limited number of players who have a lot of control over what is produced and how much the consumer must pay for the products. Examples are the automobile, pharmaceutical, and oil industries.

prompt: Springfield charges its residents a 6.5% sales tax on all consumer products purchased. Springfield's sales tax is an example of a(n) __________ tax.
explanation: Regressive. A sales tax is an example of a regressive tax. Regressive taxes result in individuals with low incomes paying a higher amount of their income in taxes than high-income earners do. A progressive tax is a tax assessed on income or business profits which results in high-income earners paying a higher tax rate than low-income earners. A capital gains tax is charged on profits made from the sale of property or assets and is an example of a progressive tax.

prompt: Devin is a very friendly, outgoing, and outspoken manager who often decides to hold spontaneous team meetings to discuss ongoing projects and brainstorming sessions. How should he adapt his management style to accommodate shy and introverted employees?
choices: Tell them they are not required to attend team meetings.
Require them to speak at the meetings to gain more confidence.
Don't encourage them to share their ideas.
Plan meetings ahead of time so they have time to prepare.
explanation: Plan meetings ahead of time so they have time to prepare. It's important for a manager to be respectful of his employees' personalities and work preferences. A manager should allow introverted employees time to prepare for meetings so they feel more comfortable sharing their ideas in front of others. It would be insensitive to require introverted employees to speak at meetings. All employees should be required to attend team meetings so they are informed about the team's activities. Telling an employee not to attend team meetings is likely to make him/her feel that s/he is unimportant and that his/her input is not desired. A manager should still encourage introverted employees to share their ideas through other methods such as email messages or project boards.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of informal recognition:
choices: An awards ceremony for scholarship winners
A pat on the back from a supervisor at work
A trophy given to the championship swim team
A wage bonus given to exemplary employees
explanation: A pat on the back from a supervisor at work. Informal recognition is praise given outside of formal systems and is often spontaneous, such as a positive comment, a pat on the back, or a high five. An awards ceremony, a trophy given to championship winners, and a wage bonus given to exemplary employees are all examples of formal recognition systems, which are usually planned and well thought out.

prompt: Tory is a new business owner offering data management services for medical records to hospitals. How can she identify what hospital administrators will expect from her service?
choices: Read patient reviews about each hospital
Entertain hospital administrators at a sporting event
Read about trends impacting the hospital industry
explanation: Read about trends impacting the hospital industry. One way to identify what clients will expect is to read about trends impacting their specific industry. Entertaining clients helps form better relationships and goodwill, but it may not help collect much detailed information. Patient reviews and financial information about a business do not provide much information that explains what a client expects from a service provider.

prompt: Why is it important to share the best techniques for performing a job task with your coworkers?
choices: Your coworkers will consider you an expert.
It will convince your boss to promote you.
It can reduce your work responsibilities.
explanation: It builds good working relationships. Helping your coworkers builds trust and teamwork, which improves your working relationships. Employees who share their knowledge build a stronger team and a positive work environment. Being helpful doesn't necessarily cause your coworkers to view you as an expert or convince your boss to promote you. When you teach your coworkers the best techniques, your team is likely to work more efficiently, but it doesn't reduce your work responsibilities.

prompt: Haley visited London and noticed carts selling chocolate-covered waffles on every corner. When she returned to her city, she considered opening her own waffle cart at home. This is an example of how
choices: reading trade publications can help you learn about trends.
products are generally only successful in one market.
traveling can help you identify trends and opportunities.
it is important to obtain a patent for your business idea.
explanation: Traveling can help you identify trends and opportunities. Assessing global trends can help entrepreneurs find opportunities for new business ventures. In Haley's case, traveling to a new city allowed her to learn about a trend that could lead to a business venture in her city. This is not an example of how products are only successful in one market. This example is not related to reading trade publications or to obtaining a patent for your business idea.

prompt: While working as a server, Delia came up with an idea for an automated payment system for restaurants. This is an example of how
choices: entrepreneurs should focus on completely new industries.
economic trends can help you identify opportunities.
work experience can lead to new business ventures.
it is unethical to copy another business's model.
explanation: Work experience can lead to new business ventures. One way that entrepreneurs determine opportunities for new business ventures is through their own work experience. Delia's work experience as a server, for example, helped her determine an opportunity to automate payments in the restaurant industry. This example is not related to economic trends. It is not true that entrepreneurs should focus on completely new industries; many entrepreneurial ventures take place within existing industries, such as in Delia's case. Finally, this example is not related to whether or not it is unethical to copy another business's model.

prompt: When planning a new venture, an entrepreneur can use __________ to clarify his/her goals and visions.
explanation: A mission statement. A mission statement is a brief summary of what a business owner wants a business to be doing. When planning a new venture, entrepreneurs develop mission statements to help guide their goals and visions into reality. Using a mission statement helps entrepreneurs stay on track and focus on what they really want to do. Financial forecasting, SWOT analyses, and competitive analyses are all important tools for entrepreneurs, but they are not as directly related to clarifying goals and vision.

prompt: Charlie has a great idea for a new website, but he isn't sure if there is a demand for it. Charlie needs to
explanation: Consult external resources. When entrepreneurs develop a new concept, they often need to consult outside sources to help solidify the idea or generate helpful feedback. If Charlie needs to find out whether there is a demand for his idea, he can consult external resources such as Internet resources, mentors, competitors, market trends, etc. Developing a business plan will not necessarily help Charlie know whether there is a demand for his idea; rather, he should know whether or not there is a demand before he develops a business plan. Filing for a patent will not help Charlie know whether there is a demand for his idea. Finally, obtaining funding will not necessarily help Charlie know whether there is demand for his idea; instead, he should know there is demand before he attempts to obtain funding.

prompt: Which part of the business plan helps entrepreneurs determine who will buy their products?
explanation: Market analysis. The market analysis is the section of the business plan that includes a description of the target market, the industry, and the competitive landscape. When defining a new venture, entrepreneurs can use the information gathered during the market analysis to further define their products, strategies, and ideas so they are a good fit for the market. The mission statement, company description, and financial projections do not help entrepreneurs determine who will buy their products because these sections do not include detailed marketing information.

prompt: What might happen if a startup hires its first employee too early?
choices: There won't be any interested candidates.
The employer will be less stressed.
The company won't be able to pay the employee.
explanation: The company won't be able to pay the employee. When trying to determine whether or not to hire an employee, a startup needs to consider whether or not it is actually ready to take on new staff. One issue that a new company might have is cash flow. The startup should be sure that it has the cash flow to pay the employee. If not, it should wait until it does. Employees are more likely to be underworked than overworked if they are hired too early. The employer will likely be more stressed if s/he isn't ready to hire and manage an employee, rather than less stressed. Hiring an employee too early does not necessarily dictate whether or not there will be any interested candidates.

prompt: Which of the following is a way to save money when selecting capital resources for a new business:
choices: Buy as little equipment as possible
Apply for a loan to pay for the equipment
explanation: Look for used equipment. One way to save money while obtaining capital resources for a new business is to purchase used equipment. Used equipment can be heavily discounted and can still function just as effectively as new equipment. Buying as little equipment as possible is not necessarily realistic because having the right equipment is an important aspect of business success. Purchasing equipment is costlier than renting equipment. Finally, applying for a loan will not necessarily help a new business save money.

prompt: Bethany wants to make sure she is making informed, intelligent decisions for her entrepreneurial venture. Bethany should
choices: form and consult an advisory board.
turn the business over to someone else.
explanation: Form and consult an advisory board. An advisory board is a group of local professionals who can help business owners run their organizations better. Entrepreneurs such as Bethany can set up and consult an advisory board to gain expertise and knowledge in different areas. This helps them run their businesses better. Becoming a business consultant will not necessarily help Bethany make informed, intelligent decisions for her entrepreneurial venture. Hiring an assistant might help Bethany with her workload, but it will not necessarily help her make informed and intelligent decisions. Turning the business over to someone else is not necessary; Bethany can run the business while consulting others to improve her knowledge and expertise.

prompt: Businesses become more complex as
explanation: They grow. As the size of a business grows, it increases its number of interconnected stakeholders and products. The more of these it has to manage, the more complex the organization becomes. Employees' leaving is not necessarily related to the complexity of a business. The level of control usually decreases as businesses become more complex. Managerial oversight also increases as the business becomes more complex.

prompt: Which of the following is a visual tool for organizing workflow:
explanation: A flow chart. A flow chart is a diagram that can be used to map out workflows in a visual way. It allows you to clearly see the steps and tasks in a workflow. While a database and a pie chart can both represent information visually, they are not as well-suited for organizing workflow as flow charts. A schedule can help you organize workflow, but it is not a visual representation of a workflow.

prompt: Matt has developed a new app. Before he launches it, he should
choices: make sure it has no issues.
test it with a focus group.
sell it to a larger company.
explanation: Test it with a focus group. Before launching a new product, Matt should test it first with a focus group that represents his target market. This will help him gather feedback and modify the app accordingly before releasing it to the public. Generating new ideas is not necessary when Matt has already developed his app. While it would be ideal to develop a product with no issues, it is not realistic to strive for perfection, or else the product will never be launched. Finally, Matt does not need to sell his app to a larger company before launching it.

prompt: Georgiana owns a restaurant, and recently, she has noticed that the staff throw away a lot of food at the end of each night. If Georgiana is able to cut back on the amount of food waste, she will likely experience
explanation: Increased success. When entrepreneurs use resources productively, they are able to cut costs, increase profits, and experience overall general success. If Georgiana can reduce the amount of food that is wasted, she will be using her resources more productively, thereby increasing her chances of success. Georgiana will not necessarily experience higher overhead costs, a damaged reputation, or a larger workforce; these are unrelated to cutting back on food waste.

prompt: When the founder of Reece Engineering Firm stepped down, the business lost several key clients and started to see its profits decline. Reece Engineering Firm could have benefitted from
explanation: Continuation planning. Continuation planning is a plan for the future of a business to ensure that it continues operating successfully when the founder or leader transitions out of his/her role. If Reece Engineering Firm had a continuation plan in place, it would have been able to prevent the loss of clients and profits that occurred when the founder stepped down. Idea generation, feasibility studies, and risktaking would not have helped Reece Engineering in this instance.

prompt: Will is ready to take a step back from ownership of his business, but he still wants to remain involved. Will should
choices: spend more time away from the office.
sell the company to a financial investor.
sell the company to an employee.
explanation: Sell the company to an employee. An internal exit from a business occurs when the business owner sells the organization to an employee. If Will wants to take a step back from ownership, but still wants to be involved, he should consider selling his business internally to an employee or manager at the company. This will allow him to remain involved and transition slowly and steadily into a new role. Selling the company to a financial investor is an external exit. Generally, it is more difficult for an owner to remain involved when the company is sold to a third party outside of the organization. Starting a competing business will not necessarily help Will take a step back while staying involved with his current business. Finally, spending more time away from the office is not a realistic solution because Will would still have responsibility for the ownership of his business.

prompt: A customer slips on a wet floor and breaks her leg while in Patti's home-based cooking business. What type of insurance coverage should Patti have that would pay the customer's medical costs?
explanation: General liability insurance. General liability insurance covers injuries to clients or employees that occur on the premises or property of a business. It is important for a home-based business owner to obtain coverage for any type of losses that may occur related to conducting business. Many home-based business activities can actually void a home insurance policy. Disability insurance provides payments to assist a business owner or employee who is unable to work due to an illness or injury. Business property insurance protects property and equipment used to conduct business.

prompt: Improved performance, reduced costs, increased profitability, and competitive advantage are most likely to be reasons why a business may choose to engage in
explanation: Business process change. There are several reasons why a company may choose to engage in business process change, including the need to improve performance, reduce costs, increase profits, or regain a competitive advantage. These benefits are not necessarily results of anti-harassment training, human resources management, or community outreach.

prompt: At the beginning of each fiscal year, Jessica analyzes financial information and performs calculations to help her business determine its financial goals (such as what to sell and how much to sell). Jessica is engaging in
explanation: Managerial accounting. Managerial accounting is a type of accounting that involves preparing and reporting financial data to internal users, usually managers, who need financial information to control dayto-day operations and to make financial decisions and plans affecting the business. In this example, Jessica is providing helpful information to her company so that it can determine its financial goals for the year. Jessica is engaging in managerial accounting, not cost-benefit analysis, financial accounting, or business consulting. A cost-benefit analysis is a process for evaluating business decisions that involves summarizing the associated costs and benefits of the potential outcomes. Financial accounting is a type of accounting that involves preparing and reporting financial data to external users who are not directly involved in business operations. Business consulting is usually performed by an individual from outside a company and involves helping a company solve problems and implement solutions.

prompt: What type of funding carries the most financial risk for a startup company that has an unsuccessful first launch of the business?
explanation: Crowdfunding. When a startup is crowdfunded, an unsuccessful launch typically causes investors to take their funds back and no longer deal with the enterprise. A business without the financial support of investors is very likely to fail. Venture capitalists, angel investors, and banks are more willing to support a struggling startup because they have access to large amounts of capital and are accustomed to the financial risks of launching businesses.

prompt: Steve is 60 years old and has retired from a job after 30 years working at a tree farm. Steve has always dreamed of running a small orchard and fruit farm. If his business fails, what type of funding carries the most personal financial risk to Steve's future?
choices: Finding a partner to help fund the business
Borrowing cash from his retirement account
Obtaining a business loan from a bank
explanation: Borrowing cash from his retirement account. It is risky for a person nearing retirement age to borrow funds from a retirement account. S/He will lose interest earnings on the borrowed funds and may never be able to repay the funds thereby putting his/her financial future at risk. A business partner reduces financial risk by sharing funds and responsibility for a business's success or failure. A bank loan carries less personal financial risk because if bankruptcy is necessary, the borrower can typically protect personal assets such as retirement accounts. A grant carries the least risk since it is free money that does not need to be repaid.

prompt: The ADKAR model, which stands for Awareness, Desire, Knowledge, Ability, and Reinforcement, is a strategy that businesses use for
explanation: Change management. ADKAR is a change management model that involves five key steps: building awareness of the reasons for change, fostering a desire to participate in the change, educating people about how to implement and adjust to the change, enabling people to actually execute the change, and reinforcing the change once it has been successfully implemented. ADKAR is not used in programmed thinking, which is a process used to solve problems and generate ideas in logical, analytical, organized ways. ADKAR is not typically used in project initiation or project management.

prompt: Sarah is applying for a business loan to finance some new equipment for her business. Why should Sarah review the business's current cash flow before calculating the actual loan amount to request?
choices: To calculate how much the equipment will cost
To determine what amount can be repaid each month
To guarantee that the bank will grant the loan
To evaluate whether the equipment is a good investment
explanation: To determine what amount can be repaid each month. To calculate the actual amount to borrow, cash flow is reviewed to determine what monthly loan payments the business can realistically pay each month. A business without enough cash flow to make loan payments is taking a significant financial business risk. The cost of purchasing equipment is negotiated with the vendor. There is no way to guarantee that a bank will grant a loan since the bank evaluates many financial and business factors impacting a business. The investment value of a purchase is not determined by a company's current cash flow.

prompt: Which of the following is a benefit of debt financing when starting a business:
choices: You have help from knowledgeable, experienced investors.
You don't need to pay interest on the money.
You have control over how the money is spent.
You don't have to pay back the money if the business fails.
explanation: You have control over how the money is spent. One of the biggest benefits of debt financing is the ability to control how the financing is spent. When you take out a business loan, you are in control of what you do with the money. When you obtain equity financing, however, the investors that are helping you start your business have primary control over business decisions. Some of the downsides of debt financing include interest payments and the need to pay the money back even if the business fails. Help from experienced investors is a benefit of equity financing, not debt financing.

prompt: A business must make monthly loan and interest payments on a piece of equipment it purchased. This is an example of a(n) __________ cost.
explanation: Recurring. Monthly loan and interest payments are an example of recurring costs—they must be paid on a regular basis. Potential costs are hidden costs managers must consider—such as what will happen if they don't make a certain choice or what will happen if the project fails. One-time costs are expenses that the business will need to pay only once. Recurring costs are not called investment costs.

prompt: The traditional approach to budgeting strategy is __________ budgeting.
explanation: Incremental. The traditional approach to budgeting strategy is known as incremental budgeting. It's a time-saving strategy, but it fails to take changing circumstances and priorities into account. Zero-based budgeting is the “answer” to the shortcomings of incremental budgeting; it involves rebuilding the budget for each new budgeting period. Flexible and short-term refer to types of budget formats, not budgeting strategies.

prompt: Which of the following ratios can help a business determine its overall profitability:
explanation: Return on equity. There are several profitability ratios that can help a business determine its overall profitability, including return on equity, profit margin, return on assets, and gross margin ratio. The return on equity ratio is a company's net income divided by its average stockholder's equity. This ratio is useful for illustrating how effective a company is at turning cash into greater gains for the company and for investors. A liquidity ratio measures a company's ability to pay off its short-term debts. A working capital ratio is a type of liquidity ratio. A dividend yield is a type of market prospect ratio. Investors use market prospect ratios to predict what the trend of a stock will be in the future.

prompt: The Ace Company's number one business priority is to develop confident and capable employees who can provide expert customer assistance. Another important business priority is to increase the company's profitability. The company's current growth is stable, but it is experiencing a high rate of employee turnover. After investigating, it's discovered that employees are overwhelmed by the complicated processes that they must learn. Which of the following actions will best help the company meet its business priorities:
choices: Fire new employees who don't perform well.
Offer higher wages so employees won't quit.
explanation: Provide ongoing employee training. To develop confident and capable employees, a company should provide training on a regular basis. Well-trained employees perform their jobs more efficiently, which in turn increases a company's profitability. Hiring more employees or offering higher wages during stable growth will reduce the company's profitability. Firing new employees will increase employee turnover and prevent the company from developing experienced employees.

prompt: The Star Company is operating at a steady level. Its main business priorities are to become more efficient and limit business costs. The Star Company uses a custom database that can only be accessed by two employees at one time. This causes many delays to the employees' projects. Updating the database to accommodate more users is costly. Which of the following short-term solutions is most likely to help the company meet its business priorities:
choices: Buy more computers for employees to use
Pay for a database update to improve employees' efficiency
Hire more employees to complete projects on time
Print the data that employees need to complete projects
explanation: Print the data that employees need to complete projects. Printing the information is a good short-term solution since employees won't need to use the database to complete their projects. It also will help the company be more efficient without increasing business costs significantly. Paying to update the database is a costly, long-term solution. Hiring more employees and buying more computers fail to solve the database's two-user limitation.

prompt: Why is it important to provide an overview of an initial training session with staff members before training begins?
choices: It helps staff members decide if they need the training.
It gives staff members the opportunity to study before training begins.
It enables staff members to succeed in the training sessions.
It lets staff members know what to expect during the training.
explanation: It lets staff members know what to expect during the training. It's a good idea to let staff members know what an initial training session involves so they understand the purpose and what will be required of them. Initial training sessions typically provide information and instruction and do not require participants to study. Telling staff what to expect during training gives them a frame of reference but does not ensure staff member success with training. Training sessions do not evaluate staff members' performance. Managers, not employees, typically determine whether staff members require training or not.

prompt: Liam has complained to his manager, Renee, that he can't complete his reports on time because the accounting department has not updated data that he needs. How should Renee respond to Liam's complaint?
choices: Tell him to report the situation to a staff member in upper management
Ignore him because he is probably making excuses for missing his deadlines
Carefully listen and ask the accounting manager to help find solutions
Personally report the situation to a staff member in upper management
explanation: Carefully listen and ask the accounting manager to help find solutions. A manager should let his/her employees know that their problems are taken seriously by carefully listening to them and looking for solutions. It's unwise to ignore employee complaints which can provide valuable information about problems impacting the company. Asking the accounting manager to help find solutions shows respect and trust by resolving the problem instead of escalating it. All employees should follow a company's chain of command by initially working with their immediate managers and coworkers to resolve problems. A manager should avoid reporting a problem to upper management until s/he has worked with others to discover and resolve issues that have caused the problem.

prompt: A company is drafting a budget for a new product it intends to sell. The data that it includes in this new product's budget are most likely to be
explanation: Estimates. Unlike hard facts, estimates are approximations of data, or educated guesses. Businesses use estimates all the time. For instance, if marketers are planning to develop a new product, they will create a budget, estimating how much money they'll need to complete each step of the development process. Facts are data that can be verified. There's no disputing that a fact is true. However, budgets do not contain facts because they are used to make predictions and estimates about the future—and nobody knows exactly what the future holds! The data in budgets are not goals, since a business's goals may differ wildly from the organization's actual expected needs or requirements. Budget information should not be false.

prompt: Which of the following best describes the type of company that benefits most from marketing research:
choices: Small businesses who wish to expand their operations
Large corporations with plans to change marketing strategies
Any business wanting to improve its decision-making abilities
Nonprofit organizations interested in their competition
explanation: Any business wanting to improve its decision-making abilities. Businesses of all sorts and sizes conduct marketing research for many reasons, including to change their marketing strategies, expand their operations, or learn about their competition. Regardless of the specific purpose, any business would benefit from marketing research because it informs and improves the business's decision-making abilities.

prompt: When it comes to buying behavior, people tend to
choices: satisfy their most urgent needs first.
purchase products contrary to their needs.
satisfy their less urgent needs first.
explanation: Satisfy their most urgent needs first. When it comes to buying behavior, consumers tend to meet their needs in an organized way. The most urgent needs are satisfied first, such as the needs for food, water, and shelter. After the most urgent needs are satisfied, consumers then move on to less urgent needs such as the needs for social belonging, achievement, or self-fulfillment. People generally do not satisfy their less urgent needs first, or purchase products contrary to their needs. Consumers usually purchase products in an organized, identifiable pattern.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a marketing goal:
explanation: Increase sales by 5%. Goals are objectives that marketers plan to fulfill. Increasing sales by 5% is what the company plans to achieve. Reducing prices is a strategy, or plan of action for achieving a goal or objective. Creating a new website and sending out an email newsletter could be considered tactics, or ways a company could carry out its strategy.

prompt: Green Glow Cosmetics decides that its new purifying face masks will be targeted to females ages 16-25. Green Glow Cosmetics is segmenting the market based on
explanation: Demographics. Demographic segmentation divides a market on the basis of its physical and social characteristics, including gender, origin or heritage, religion, socioeconomic status, and life stage. Green Glow Cosmetics is focusing on a demographic segment of the market—females ages 16-25. Geographic segmentation is based on location. Psychographic segmentation is based on customers' lifestyles and personalities. Behavioral segmentation is based on dividing customers into groups according to their response to a product.

prompt: Gabrielle used to own the only coffee shop in her neighborhood, but another shop just opened up down the street. This competition is considered a
explanation: Threat. A threat is any unfavorable situation in the environment surrounding a business. If Gabrielle faces a competitor who may take away some of her customers, that's definitely an unfavorable situation. A weakness is any limitation or shortcoming a business has that can keep it from achieving its objectives. An opportunity is any favorable situation in the environment surrounding a business. A strength is any resource or capability a business has that can help it gain a competitive advantage in its industry.

prompt: A company needs to forecast sales for its yearly marketing plan. The business decides to use a type of forecasting in which several experts are asked for their opinions. In other words, the business is utilizing the __________ method of sales forecasting.
explanation: Jury of executive opinion. The jury of executive opinion is a qualitative sales forecasting method that gathers opinions from company executives (or other experts) to help predict sales. Under the salesforce opinion method, salespeople make sales estimates for their territories for a specific time period. The test marketing method involves introducing products to a geographic area for a limited time and studying sales results. The market factor analysis method involves studying factors that may impact sales such as the economy, the legal environment, and current trends.

prompt: Brian is developing a customer profile for his new dog-sitting company's target market. Which of the following questions is most relevant for developing his customer profile:
choices: What challenges do my potential customers face when caring for their dog(s)?
What do my potential customers enjoy doing in their free time?
Why did my potential customers choose to get a dog in the first place?
What is my potential customers' job or occupation?
explanation: What challenges do my potential customers face when caring for their dog(s)? One of the most important steps in developing a customer profile is determining the specific challenges that the target customers face in regards to the business's services/products. Brian should determine what challenges his potential customers face before starting his dog-sitting business so that he can tailor his services to his target market. Determining what customers do in their free time, what they do for a living, and the reasons behind their choice to get a dog may also help develop a customer profile, but they are not necessarily as relevant as determining the customers' challenges in caring for their dog(s).

prompt: A retail store tracks the number of customers that open the company's promotional emails and/or visit its website. The company uses these data to measure its marketing performance. Which of the following marketing metrics is the company using:
explanation: Customer engagement patterns. Customer engagement data, such as email-open rates and social media activity, are useful for measuring marketing success when tied to purchasing behavior. This example demonstrates the use of customer engagement patterns as a marketing metric, not predictive analytics, customer acquisition cost, or predictive revenue. Predictive analytics measure purchase-related behaviors, such as the length of time between purchases or which assortment of products a customer tends to browse before making a final purchase. Customer acquisition cost is a metric that determines how much money it costs to convince a customer to make a purchase. Predictive revenue is a marketing metric that involves calculating predicted future revenues.

prompt: Why is it important for a business's stored business records to be accurate?
choices: They can be kept secure from data breaches.
They need to be accurate when shared with other businesses.
They can safely be stored for long periods of time.
They need to be reliable for making business decisions.
explanation: They need to be reliable for making business decisions. It's important for a business to keep accurate records so it can rely on the information to make good business decisions. A business's records are considered private and are not typically shared with other businesses. A business record's accuracy is determined by the users who create and maintain it, not by how long or securely it is stored.

prompt: What type of information in a company's CRM system can help a company determine a customer's product preferences?
explanation: Customer's prior purchases. A CRM system can keep records of sales history, which can help a company determine a customer's product preferences. CRM systems also store many other types of data such as a customer's contact and payment methods. A customer's name, address, or preferred payment method provides very few clues to determine his/her product preferences.

prompt: Which of the following is most likely a potential safety issue in the workplace:
choices: A cell phone ban during work hours
explanation: Cluttered, over-stacked warehouses. One potential cause of safety hazards is a cluttered, over-stacked warehouse. Clutter can make it difficult for employees to access emergency exits and can cause issues with sprinkler systems, for example. These issues can put employees at risk. Chatty employees who converse frequently, a cell phone ban during work hours, and a small parking lot are not necessarily potential safety issues.

prompt: Quincy came up with a great idea for a new product and hired his friend Kendra to be his partner in starting a new business. However, after learning all about his new product idea, Kendra used the information she learned to obtain a position with a competing company. Quincy should have
choices: refrained from hiring in the first place.
obtained a trademark for his idea.
asked Kendra to sign a nondisclosure agreement.
explanation: Asked Kendra to sign a nondisclosure agreement. A nondisclosure agreement is a legal document that prevents an employee from sharing confidential information about a company with anyone. A nondisclosure agreement would have prevented Kendra from using the information she learned while working for Quincy to get a job with a competitor. Obtaining a trademark or backing up data digitally would not have helped Quincy in this instance. Refraining from hiring in the first place is not necessarily realistic, and any employee he eventually hired could have done the same thing without a nondisclosure agreement in place.

prompt: Cody works for a large paintbrush manufacturer. Cody is selecting a vendor to provide all the plastic needed to produce handles for its paintbrushes. Which of the following is the first step Cody should take to conduct a formal selection process:
choices: Contact the former supplier to ensure continued business
Document what types of plastic are required
Meet with several suppliers to evaluate their offerings
explanation: Document what types of plastic are required. The first step of the vendor selection process is documenting the specifications needed for the supplies, materials, or products to be purchased. The first step is important because it helps identify whether the vendors' offerings will meet the company's needs. Identifying potential suppliers is the second step of the vendor selection process. The third step is meeting with several suppliers to evaluate their offerings for the best material, service, price, and to identify a backup supplier. It is unwise to rely on a former supplier when a significant purchasing decision is being made that will have a large impact on the company.

prompt: When creating a quality assurance program, it is important that a manager first
explanation: Creates standards. Management can help work toward the achievement of quality by implementing a quality assurance plan. The first step of putting together a quality assurance plan is to create quality standards. These standards help define quality and give the program a basis for functioning. Before a manager implements corrective action, trains staff, or puts together a quality committee, s/he needs to create quality standards.

prompt: Callie wants to know when her business will start generating a profit. She already knows her fixed costs and has set her prices. To conduct break-even analysis, Callie next needs to
explanation: Determine variable costs. One of the most important considerations in break-even analysis is variable costs—recurring costs that come with manufacturing a product and change depending on how many products are produced. Callie needs to estimate her variable costs in order to know how much she needs to sell to start generating a profit. Callie does not necessarily need to cut overhead costs, choose a new pricing method, or select a target market to conduct break-even analysis.

prompt: One way to gain more negotiating power when leasing a business space is to
choices: settle on a rate of rent increase.
choose a market that has plenty of space available.
share the office space with another business.
explanation: Choose a market that has plenty of space available. When leasing a property, if the market is hot and there are limited spaces available, it will be more difficult for tenants to gain any negotiating power because of competition. Landlords can easily turn down requests because there are many other potential tenants. However, if the market has plenty of space available, the tenant has more negotiating power. There are many other options that the tenant could choose, so the landlord will be more willing to negotiate terms. Focusing on a short-term lease, settling on a rate of rent increase, or sharing the office space with another business are all important factors to discuss when negotiating leases, but they will not necessarily affect the negotiating power of the business.

prompt: One of the primary goals of supply chain management is to
choices: minimize overall value to the customer.
gain a competitive advantage in the marketplace.
set prices for products that maximize profits.
control customer perceptions of a business.
explanation: Gain a competitive advantage in the marketplace. Supply chain management involves supervising the complete process of getting products into the marketplace, from production to purchase by an end consumer. Two of the main goals of supply chain management are maximizing the value that is provided to the customer and gaining a competitive advantage in the marketplace by moving goods effectively and efficiently. Setting prices and controlling customer perceptions are not primary goals of supply chain management.

prompt: A university wants to attract more out-of-state/province students. To help it determine the best course of action, the school hired a consultant who specializes in education marketing. The consultant will help the university determine its goals, overcome its obstacles in reaching out-of-state/province students, and implement a plan of action. In other words, the consultant will engage in
explanation: Business analysis. Business analysts help organizations introduce and manage change—such as reaching a new target market or implementing a new marketing strategy. In this example, the university hired a business analyst to help it reach its goal of attracting out-of-state/province students. The consultant in this example is not engaging in managerial accounting, which is a type of accounting used to help company leadership make financial decisions. The consultant may use SWOT analysis (identifying a company's strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats) to support the overall consulting process, but business analysis is a better way to define the consultant's services. A costbenefit analysis is a process for evaluating business decisions that involves summarizing the associated costs and benefits of the potential outcomes.

prompt: Business process thinking is beneficial for project management because documented processes
explanation: Can be analyzed and repeated. Business process thinking means thinking about a project or an assignment in terms of the processes that will be required to complete it. One of the primary benefits of process thinking is the ability to document (and then refine and repeat) the processes that are involved in a project. By documenting a process, the process can be improved and standardized so that the best possible results are achieved. Process thinking does not guarantee a project's success, but it does improve its chances. Process thinking results in more efficient projects, not less efficient projects.

prompt: A company is caught off guard when its international headquarters is suddenly caught in the middle of a gunfight between government officials and rebel groups. While rebel protesters occupy the company's building, the company must decide how to protect its employees while remaining neutral. This example demonstrates how __________ affect risk management.
explanation: Political disturbances. There are several factors that can influence risk management in other countries, including the potential for political disturbances, weak foreign economies, emerging technologies, and sudden changes in international regulations. In this example, political unrest caused a potentially dangerous situation for the company whose building was occupied. Companies should carefully plan for situations such as this when creating risk management strategies.

prompt: A manufacturer uses software to run its production lines that can only operate on a maximum of 15 separate production lines at once. This is an example of a(n) __________ factor influencing process design.
explanation: Technology. There are many factors influencing business process design, including technology, human factors (such as morale and stress), regulatory changes, and environmental factors (such as competition and trends). This example demonstrates how technology can impact a process, not how human factors, regulatory factors, or environmental factors can impact a process.

prompt: Which of the following statements regarding managerial accounting is true:
choices: The goal of managerial accounting is to provide information to users within a company, not outside of it.
Managerial accounting aims to provide accurate financial information to stockholders, creditors, and other external parties.
The goal of managerial accounting is to provide information to relevant parties according to financial regulations.
Managerial accounting places emphasis on the past, unlike financial accounting which places
explanation: The goal of managerial accounting is to provide information to users within a company, not outside of it. Managerial accounting involves providing financial information to users within a company (generally company management) for the purpose of helping the company make decisions. Managerial accounting does not provide information to users outside of the company, such as stockholders, creditors, or other external parties. Because managerial accounting provides information solely to internal sources, it does not have to comply with regulations like financial accounting does. Managerial accountants provide information to help a company make decisions in the future, while financial accounting generally provides information about the past.

prompt: Which of the following statements regarding the relationship between a business and its supply chain is true:
choices: A business's supply chain has very little impact on the business's overall success.
If a business's supply chain is poorly managed, customer satisfaction is likely to suffer.
Effective supply chain management results in lower customer satisfaction.
Supply chains with organizational problems tend to boost members' overall success.
explanation: If a business's supply chain is poorly managed, customer satisfaction is likely to suffer. A business's supply chain has a large impact on the business's overall success. One of the ways that poor supply chain management can negatively impact a business is through decreasing customer satisfaction. Companies that can't effectively distribute their products to consumers will likely lose many of their customers. Effective supply chain management, on the other hand, generally results in higher customer satisfaction because products are distributed quickly and effectively. Supply chains with organizational problems tend to hurt business success, not boost it.

prompt: Anti-malware protection, encryption, routine backups, and operating system updates are all effective tools for
explanation: Protecting digital assets. Businesses should take the appropriate steps to protect their digital assets, such as customer data and financial information. Some of the most effective methods for protecting data include using anti-malware tools, encrypting sensitive data, backing up important information, and updating operating systems regularly. These tools are not necessarily helpful for screening potential employees, organizing customer information, or sorting through financial data.

prompt: Which of the following is a benefit of using time-management skills to prioritize tasks:
choices: It reduces the time needed to complete tasks.
It eliminates errors from being made.
It helps you arrive at events on time.
explanation: It minimizes procrastination. Prioritizing tasks helps you focus on the most important ones and eliminate the tendency to put them off until a later date. Prioritizing tasks does not reduce the amount of time needed to complete tasks, eliminate errors, or improve punctuality. Planning and scheduling tools are time-management techniques that can help you become punctual.

prompt: Who is in charge of deciding how much a company's CEO will be paid?
explanation: The board of directors. The board of directors is in charge of making many important decisions for a company. One of those is deciding how much the company's CEO will be paid. Company shareholders, employees, and the CEO are not in charge of deciding how much the CEO will be paid.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of transparency in corporate governance:
choices: Embellishing or exaggerating company success to shareholders
Communicating goals and strategies to top management only
Releasing financial documents only if pressured to by shareholders
Promptly disclosing financial information to shareholders
explanation: Promptly disclosing financial information to shareholders. Transparency in corporate governance means being honest, clear, and timely when communicating important information to company stakeholders. A company should promptly release financial information to its shareholders, not wait to release the information until it is under pressure. Goals and strategies should be widely communicated, not only to top managers. Companies should never embellish or exaggerate company success to shareholders.

prompt: Objective setting, risk assessment, and risk response are all components of
explanation: Enterprise risk management. Enterprise risk management (ERM) is a comprehensive risk management strategy that involves planning for both physical and business risks. Steps involved in ERM include setting corporate objectives, assessing potential risks, and determining appropriate responses to risks. These are not primary steps in asset allocation strategies, channel-management plans, or conflict resolution policies. Asset allocation involves diversifying one's investments by type (equity, fixed-income, cash etc.). Channel management is a process by which marketers ensure that products are distributed to customers efficiently and effectively. Conflict resolution is the process of resolving or ending a conflict.

prompt: A bicycle manufacturer has sold the same bike for more than 15 years. During that time, the price of the bike has fluctuated according to changes in the economy, pressure from competing brands, and consumer trends. In other words, the manufacturer's pricing strategies have been __________ over time.
explanation: Flexible. Marketers must understand that the prices they set are written on paper—not in stone. Because pricing is a tug-of-war and a constant quest for balance, businesses must be willing to adjust their prices as necessary. These adjustments may be increases or decreases, depending on the circumstances the business faces. Prices should also be realistic (in-line with what customers expect to pay) and competitive (able to compete with the prices of other companies). Prices should never be rigid or set in stone.

prompt: A wholesaler sells its products at a much lower price to its largest retailer than it sells its products to its smallest retailer. This is an illegal practice known as
explanation: Price discrimination. Price discrimination is an illegal activity in which a business charges different customers different prices for similar amounts and types of products. Price fixing is an illegal business agreement in which competing businesses agree on prices of their goods or services, resulting in little choice for the consumer. Bait-and-switch advertising involves promoting a low-priced item to attract customers to whom the business then tries to sell a higher priced item. Unit pricing is a legal pricing technique in which consumers are given the price per unit (pound, ounce, etc.) for products.

prompt: A bank offers various types of consumer financial products, including home loans, checking accounts, and savings accounts. This group of similar products is an example of a product
explanation: Line. A product line is a group of related product items. The product items in a product line are somewhat like the members of a family in their relationship to each other; they often resemble each other in some way. A company's product mix is the particular assortment of products a business offers to meet its market's needs and its company's goals. A bank's product mix would include all of its offerings, not just its consumer financial products. A product item is each individual good, service, or idea that a business offers for sale. A product category generally refers to the specific way that a product is classified. Products may be categorized in various ways, according to distribution method, customer group, or price.

prompt: A restaurant allows customers to order via its website and pay via tablet computers at each table. The restaurant is using __________ to provide excellent customer service.
explanation: Technology. Technology itself is not customer service; instead, it is a tool for supporting and serving customers. A website that allows customers to order and tablets that allow customers to pay are technological conveniences that help provide great customer service. The restaurant is not using competition, cross training, or internal service to provide excellent customer service.

prompt: A unique selling proposition often forms the basis for a company's
explanation: Promotional campaign. A unique selling proposition often forms the basis for a company's promotional campaign. The company's marketers use the USP as a way to catch customers' attention and show them the unique benefits of the product. Research and development should come before a USP. A USP doesn't necessarily affect a company's projected budget or hiring practices.

prompt: Which of the following is considered a post-purchase touchpoint:
explanation: Warranties. Touchpoints typically fall into one of three categories: pre-purchase, purchase, and postpurchase. Pre-purchase touchpoints are those that occur before a sales transaction. Your business's advertising, your website, and word-of-mouth recommendations are pre-purchase touchpoints. Purchase touchpoints, as you may have figured out, take place during a sales transaction. These touchpoints include customers' visits to your store and conversations with salespeople. Post-purchase touchpoints occur after the sale. Warranties, rebates, and customer satisfaction surveys fall into this category.

prompt: Effective promotional communication is
explanation: Persuasive. Successful promotion convinces potential customers that the product being offered for sale can satisfy their specific needs. Promotional communication should also be relevant to the target audience; appropriate for the product, image, or idea; and repetitive so that customers remember the message.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of specialty media frequently used to advertise a business:
choices: A pen with a logo on it
explanation: A pen with a logo on it. Specialty media remind people about a business. An item must pass three criteria to qualify as specialty media: 1) It must have the business's name or logo on it; 2) It must be a useful item such as a pen or baseball cap; and 3) It must be given away. A magazine is a type of publication, not a specialty media. A billboard is an example of out-of-home media. Mailed advertisements are direct mail, not specialty media.

prompt: A book publisher provides free copies of its newest releases to a handful of book reviewers in the hopes that they will spread the word about the books to their followers. This is an example of __________ marketing.
explanation: Grassroots. Grassroots marketing efforts start from the ground up, targeting a specific group of people in the hopes that the group will spread the message to a larger population. Providing free products to a targeted group is an example of grassroots marketing. Mass marketing, also known as undifferentiated marketing, involves designing products and directing marketing activities to appeal to the whole market. Viral marketing uses social media networks to encourage the sharing of promotional material. Scarcity marketing involves controlling the amount of a product that is available to a market, so that desire for the product is increased.

prompt: Rebecca receives so many promotional phone calls that she has placed her phone number on several “Do Not Call” registries. This example demonstrates
choices: the need for direct marketers to disregard "do not call" lists.
that direct marketing is a useless form of promotion.
the potential for consumer overload in direct marketing.
how direct marketing does more harm than good.
explanation: The potential for consumer overload in direct marketing. Direct marketing, such as telemarketing and email marketing, is a form of promotion that involves contacting customers directly with targeted messages. Direct marketing is not entirely useless, since it can be an effective way to inform customers about a brand or product. However, one of the biggest cons of direct marketing is the potential for consumer overload. When customers get inundated with marketing messages, they often stop paying attention to them. Direct marketers should be strategic with their promotional messages so that customers do not get bored or irritated. Marketers should always respect “do not call” lists.

prompt: Martin is in the checkout line at the grocery store when he sees an eye-catching display of candy bars. He realizes that he's hungry, so he grabs one for the ride home. The candy bar display in the checkout aisle is an example of
explanation: Point-of-sale marketing. Point-of-sale marketing is marketing that occurs at the location where products are sold to the final consumer. A display of candy bars in the checkout aisle is an example of point-ofsale marketing. A free-standing insert is a piece of paper that is placed in a newspaper or magazine, usually containing marketing materials such as coupons. A sweepstakes is a type of contest in which prizes are awarded to winners. Trade-in promotions allow customers to trade a used product for cash or gift cards.

prompt: Which of the following statements correctly describes a difference between advertising and sales promotions:
choices: Sales promotions and advertising are two words used to describe the same thing.
Sales promotions can be subtle and indirect, whereas advertising is more to-the-point.
Advertising is a short-term activity, whereas sales promotions are typically long-term.
Sales promotions typically have a limited time frame, whereas advertising is ongoing.
explanation: Sales promotions typically have a limited time frame, whereas advertising is ongoing. Sales promotions are generally short-term in nature and are intended to sell as many products as possible within a specific time frame. Advertising, on the other hand, is a long-term activity that takes place in various places and at various times to communicate a desired message. Advertising can be subtle and indirect, whereas promotions are generally to-the-point and clear. While similar, advertising and sales promotion are not the same thing.

prompt: Mel, a public relations specialist, recently updated her clients' web pages to include keywords and phrases that are frequently looked up on Google. In other words, Mel utilized __________ to improve her clients' web pages.
explanation: Search engine optimization. Search engine optimization, or SEO, is a valuable tool for public relations. SEO involves using keywords and phrases on a company's web pages so that search engines like Google can easily find them and use them as search results. RSS is a technology that allows individuals to receive updates from their favorite websites as they are posted. Many people subscribe to RSS feeds to get updates from websites without having to constantly search for new information. Email marketing involves sending promotional emails to customers. Web monitoring is not generally a term used to describe a public relations strategy.

prompt: Which of the following is the best example of an interactive public relations activity:
explanation: Press conference. There are two basic types of public relations activities: interactive and one-way. Interactive public relations activities allow for communication between an organization and the public to flow both ways, whereas one-way activities involve one-way communication from an organization to the public. Examples of interactive public relations activities include press conferences, speaking engagements, sponsorships, blogs, chat rooms, and social media. Examples of one-way public relations activities typically include search engine optimization, newsletters, websites, podcasts, press releases, and direct mail.

prompt: Which of the following focuses primarily on preventing defective products from being created:
explanation: Quality assurance. Quality control is a process that measures products against predetermined standards after the products have already been created. If a product is defective (doesn't meet standards), it can be weeded out and discarded or possibly repaired. Quality assurance, on the other hand, is an organizationwide system that businesses use to ensure that products meet quality standards. It includes quality control, but its scope is much bigger than just that. With quality control or inspection, defective products are identified only after they've been created. Quality assurance, however, seeks to prevent defective products from being created in the first place. Quality management is the ongoing process of planning, implementing, and integrating quality into every aspect of an organization. Quality improvement involves an organization's willingness to change and adapt for the purpose of maintaining quality.

prompt: Which of the following statements regarding risk and business objectives is true:
choices: Businesses should focus primarily on mitigating risks rather than meeting goals.
Businesses that have good corporate objectives do not need to plan for risks.
Risk management should not be considered when planning corporate strategy.
Good business plans aim to meet corporate goals while mitigating risks.
explanation: Good business plans aim to meet corporate goals while mitigating risks. Effective strategic plans focus equally on meeting corporate goals and planning for potential risks. Businesses that have good corporate objectives should still plan for potential risks, since risks can seriously harm a company's ability to meet its objectives. Risk management and goal achievement should both be priorities when planning corporate strategy. Businesses should focus equally on meeting goals and mitigating risks.

prompt: KRM Corporation has several safeguards in place to protect itself from both physical hazards (fires, floods, earthquakes, etc.) and business hazards such as technology failure and supply chain problems. Each year, its managers meet to reassess the relevant risks to the business and reevaluate the company's plans in the event of those risks. KRM Corporation is practicing
explanation: Enterprise risk management. Enterprise risk management (ERM) is a comprehensive risk management strategy that involves planning for both physical and business risks. The company in this example is practicing ERM, not a cost-benefit analysis, security assessment training, or hazardous circumstance planning. Cost-benefit analysis is a process for evaluating business decisions that involves summarizing the associated costs and benefits of the potential outcomes. Security assessment training and hazardous circumstance planning are not terms commonly used to describe risk management.

prompt: Internal and external controls, policies, and guidelines for reaching goals while meeting stakeholders' needs are all common elements of
explanation: Corporate governance structures. An effective corporate governance strategy combines controls, policies, and guidelines to ensure that the organization is reaching its objectives while meeting its stakeholders' needs. Common examples of controls, policies, and guidelines include performance measurement systems, audits, separation of power within the governance structure, and clearly defined communication lines. Controls and policies can also be external, such as legal regulations for business. Policies and guidelines are also important for driving an organization toward its goals. Controls, policies, and guidelines are not necessarily the primary elements of public relations strategies, legal regulations for businesses, or nondisclosure agreements.

prompt: It is particularly challenging for companies to assess external business risks because such risks are
choices: usually predictable and in the companies' control.
primarily due to factors within the company itself.
often the result of poor corporate governance.
generally unpredictable and out of the companies' control.
explanation: Generally unpredictable and out of the companies' control. External business risks such as natural disasters, economic downturns, and changes in legal regulations are generally unpredictable and out of a company's control. External business risks are the result of factors outside of a business, not the result of factors within the company itself (such as poor corporate governance).

prompt: The marketing function of selling involves __________ communication.
explanation: Planned. Selling is planned communication. That doesn't mean that salespeople read off scripts— instead, it means that salespeople have spent time learning about their products and figuring out what clients want and need. Selling is also personal communication, meaning that it should be tailored to each unique customer.

prompt: A manager evaluates future production and sales forecasts to arrange having production materials available as needed. What function of management is s/he performing?
explanation: Planning. Planning is the management function of deciding what work will be done and how it will be accomplished. Planning involves setting goals, identifying necessary resources and methods of achieving those goals, and determining dates for completing tasks and projects. Directing is the management function of providing guidance to workers and work projects. Organizing is the management function of setting up the way the business's work will be done. Controlling is the management function that monitors the work effort.

prompt: Ben's company recently acquired another company in its industry. Since the merger, Ben's management decisions have been influenced by the changes in his staff and the incorporation of new policies. What factor is most likely to be influencing Ben's management decisions?
explanation: Structural transformations. There are many factors that influence management decisions. Mergers and acquisitions are examples of structural transformations that can significantly influence a manager's decision-making. Competition in the industry, economic factors, and regulatory changes are also influential factors, but they are not demonstrated in this example.

prompt: An ice cream company is conducting an organizational SWOT. How should it categorize a new and popular trend of individually wrapped ice cream novelties?
explanation: Opportunity. An opportunity might come from new types of products or business that a company can pursue. A popular trend that is within a business's ability to produce is an example of an opportunity. Strengths typically relate to activities that a company excels at such as building a good reputation, offering value to customers, or providing excellent customer service. A weakness refers to a company's limitations such as small staff, poor cash flow, or unavailable resources. A threat refers to changes in the business environment such as competition or new technologies with which the business is unprepared to deal.

prompt: Annika develops a 40-page business plan and realizes that it includes lengthy sentences and paragraphs, along with information that is not important to her business plan's main goal. Which step for creating an effective business plan did Annika forget?
choices: Plan for regular review, updates, and corrections.
Make the plan clear and concise.
explanation: Make the plan clear and concise. Content, not length, is the most important factor for a business plan, and readers must be able to easily understand your main points. Just because the plan includes lengthy sentences and paragraphs, along with excess information, does not mean the plan is not realistic or accurate. It also doesn't mean Annika isn't planning for regular reviews, updates, and corrections.

prompt: When employees are exposed to a variety of different ideas and perspectives, they are more likely to come up with their own new ideas and strategies. In other words, knowledge and learning lead to
explanation: Innovation. Innovation, the creation or discovery of something new, such as a new product, strategy, or process, is closely tied to knowledge and learning. When employees are constantly learning at work, they are more likely to innovate. They are not more likely to become complacent, which means feeling satisfied with less-than-stellar performance. Learning and knowledge may also lead to greater curiosity and leadership, but this example specifically references innovation.

prompt: What does it mean to obtain sponsorship within the organization during the change management process?
choices: Obtaining funding for the change from an external sponsor
Securing the approval and involvement of senior executives
Gaining acceptance of the change from company stockholders
Earning the support of other companies in the industry
explanation: Securing the approval and involvement of senior executives. One of the most important steps in the change management process is obtaining sponsorship from senior executives. When company managers “sponsor” a change, they not only accept and approve of the change, they actively participate in bringing about the change. Sponsorship is critical for successful change management. Sponsorship in change management does not mean obtaining funding from an external sponsor, gaining acceptance from stockholders, or earning the support of other companies.

prompt: Why is it important for a business owner to invest his/her own personal capital into a business when applying for a business loan?
choices: It guarantees that the loan will be paid.
It shows that the business has a positive cash flow.
It increases the cash flow of the business.
explanation: It demonstrates the owner's commitment. An owner's equity (an owner's personal financial investment in a business) is a key financial used to evaluate a business's loan worthiness.
